candidate_decisions.reason: The trusted channel's seven focus branches form a coherent speech-at-old-age reading, and 17:24 independently turns the childhood-care memory into lowered, merciful conduct. The endpoint branch remains qualified; the channel is bounded by that evidence.

Every HFT trace coordinate and root matches the supplied 17:23-24 surfaces and returns to a focus word. Remembered nurture and lowered protection add a life-course relation distinct from the channel's speech contrast; all trace roles are retained as attributed evidence.

The focus's prohibited and commanded speech is followed by supplied inward knowledge, soundness, return, and forgiveness in 17:25. The inferred repair link and its general-reassurance alternative are both preserved as attributed readings.

The complete trace links parental ihsan to kin entitlement, speech when material giving is unavailable, opposed spending extremes, capacity, and balance. These exact pericope cues support calibrated care while the alternative that they are adjacent duties remains explicit.

The focus's birth-root names parents and the supplied 17:31 surface names offspring, while fear, killing, and provision make the opposite dependency pressure concrete. The common non-disposability principle is retained as the HFT reader's inference, not as an equation of the two duties.

The exact reaching verb recurs at the focus's old-age threshold and 17:34's orphan maturity threshold; the supplied custody, fulfilment, and covenant cues support a bounded stewardship analogy. Its alternative of merely coordinating distinct legal thresholds remains visible.

The focus's utterance and rebuke return in 17:36's prohibition on pursuing what is unknown and its accountability for hearing, sight, and heart. The family-specific application is retained with the HFT's general-testimony alternative.

The focus's 'at you' and opening lordship return in 17:38-39 as 'at your Lord', revealed wisdom, and exclusive worship. These concrete bookends support the attributed household-accountability reading while the whole-command-list alternative remains intact.

The attributed trace preserves the grammatical dual 'both' and uses the next ayah's wing and lowering only as independent triggers for a bounded harbor analogy. Its form-distance is stated rather than used to suppress a reading that passes the contextual test.

The focus's rebuke-to-noble-speech sequence meets the pericope's expansion, restriction, and balance imagery. The root-distance and material-flow analogy are explicitly bounded and retained as exploratory attributed evidence.

findings.title: Speech at the Old-Age Threshold
findings.claim: At the old-age threshold, the focus's contrast between a small disgust sound, forceful rebuke, and noble speech makes treatment of the now-vulnerable parents audible in the child's words. The next ayah extends that restraint into lowered, merciful conduct and prayer.
findings.mechanism: The focus names the parents, their reaching old age in the addressee's presence, and the movement from blocked contempt and rebuke to speech that confers honor. The independent trigger in 17:24 recalls the addressee's childhood dependence and commands a lowered posture and mercy; that remembered care turns the speech contrast into the opening act of care returned.
findings.reader_payoff: A brief sound and a noble utterance become opposite ways of treating vulnerable people, while the sequel shows that restraint also has a bodily form.
findings.containment: This does not establish that every caregiving role fully reverses or that status is the sole reason for kindness. The endpoint branch is qualified; gratitude and mercy remain compatible readings, and 17:24 does not prove a single motive.

epistemic.reason: The channel and its supports are trusted and the 17:24 surface is supplied; the endpoint branch is qualified and the return-care relation is contextual.

findings.title: Nurture Reversed Across a Life
findings.claim: The immediate move from parents reaching old age to the addressee's memory of being raised while small turns the duty from status-based deference into care returned across a life course: the now-stronger child lowers the body and asks mercy for former caregivers.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies parents and old age; 17:24 supplies childhood smallness, parental nurture, lowering, mercy, and prayer. Their contact changes the before-reading of deference into an attributed developmental reversal, while retaining gratitude as a live alternative.
findings.reader_payoff: The care command becomes reciprocal in time: the child once carried by the parents now offers protection as their dependency changes.
findings.containment: This is the legacy-unbound HFT reader's inference from supplied surfaces and roles, not an independently authored lexical claim. The trace at 17:24 word 11 records root ر ب و while its mapped root_000537/B005 record is headed ر ب ب; that growth contribution remains attributed and qualified. Simple gratitude without a full role-reversal model remains possible.

epistemic.reason: All trace coordinates and source roots agree with supplied occurrences and the reading returns to focus, but the HFT identity is legacy-unbound and one mapped root record differs in its displayed root.

findings.title: Speech Within a Repairable Practice
findings.claim: The focus's ban on harmful speech remains absolute, while 17:25 places filial conduct within inward knowledge, sound intention, repeated return, and forgiveness; a lapse can be repaired without turning the prohibition into permission.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the contrast between the focus's small disgust sound, overt speech, and commanded speech. The immediate trigger is 17:25's knowledge of what lies within, its condition of soundness, and forgiveness for those who repeatedly return; their contact moves the reading from an external speech threshold alone to an inward and repeatable repair practice.
findings.reader_payoff: Respectful wording is not reduced to polished sound: the inward orientation and the possibility of returning after failure remain perceptible.
findings.containment: The arrow from 17:25's general reassurance to repair after specifically filial speech lapses is the legacy-unbound reader's inference. The live alternative is that 17:25 offers general reassurance without modeling such lapses; neither reading weakens the ban on harmful speech.

epistemic.reason: The supplied ayah coordinates and roots match the attributed trace, but the repair application and its return to filial speech are reader inferences.

findings.title: Care Within Real Measure
findings.claim: The pericope lets parental ihsan read as active excellence within real capacity: kin have an owed right, accessible speech can continue care when material giving is unavailable, and measured provision rules out both withholding and self-defeating excess.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies ihsan toward parents. The independent sequence of 17:26, 17:28-30, and 17:35 places that care beside an entitlement, easy speech under inability, opposed hand positions, restricted provision, and a just balance. This contact changes open-ended generosity into owed but calibrated care without reducing excellence to a bare minimum.
findings.reader_payoff: Care can remain generous and dignifying when money is limited, because speech and measured provision are both part of the sequence.
findings.containment: The link from duties to relatives and other recipients back to parental ihsan is the HFT reader's inference; those ayat may also state adjacent duties. Balance limits material expenditure, not the obligation to treat parents well.

epistemic.reason: The listed roots and coordinates match supplied native surfaces, while the application of adjacent duties as specifications of parental ihsan remains attributed.

findings.title: Care Across Generations
findings.claim: The focus's parents at the late-life pole and 17:31's children under poverty pressure form two directions of family dependency; the HFT reading hears a shared prohibition on treating a dependent generation as disposable when care becomes costly.
findings.mechanism: The focus's birth relation names parents; 17:31 repeats that root for offspring and adds fear of poverty, killing, and divine provision. The independent opposite-generation trigger changes the before-reading of a one-way duty into a bounded principle of protection across generations.
findings.reader_payoff: The neighboring family commands can be perceived as guarding vulnerable people at opposite ends of a shared dependency relation.
findings.containment: The anti-disposability rule is the legacy-unbound reader's synthesis. The text does not equate care for aging parents with the distinct prohibition concerning children; both readings remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The same supplied birth-root appears in the focus and 17:31, but the unifying rule is an attributed inference and the two duties remain distinct.

findings.title: Two Thresholds of Stewardship

findings.mechanism: The same supplied reaching root returns with a different destination: old age in the focus, mature strength in 17:34. The orphan's protected property, the command to fulfil, and the maintained covenant trigger a contextual analogy that changes a one-way kindness reading into responsibility bounded by vulnerability and eventual maturity.
findings.reader_payoff: Power over someone dependent appears temporary and answerable, whether it concerns an aging parent or an orphan nearing maturity.
findings.containment: The HFT reader supplies the stewardship analogy; the two ayat can also coordinate distinct legal thresholds without equating parental care and orphan custody. The trace is legacy-unbound, and its application remains attributed.

epistemic.reason: The repeated reaching root and context coordinates are supplied, while the extension from orphan custody to parental stewardship is attributed.

findings.title: Speech Under Epistemic Restraint
findings.claim: Beside the focus's rule for speech to aging parents, 17:36 adds an epistemic brake: noble speech also refuses to harden partial perception or frustration into a confident verdict.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's overt saying and forceful rebuke. The independent trigger is 17:36's ban on pursuing what is not known and its naming of hearing, sight, heart, and accountability; their contact changes respectful wording alone into disciplined judgment as well as tone.
findings.reader_payoff: Listening and uncertainty become part of care, not merely the choice of a gentle phrase.
findings.containment: The return from a general rule about knowledge and accountability specifically to family speech is the legacy-unbound HFT reader's inference. A general testimony-and-belief reading remains live; the focus still independently requires noble speech.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 17:36 coordinates match supplied surfaces; the specific application to frustration with parents remains attributed.

findings.containment: The household-specific extension is the HFT reader's inference. The 17:38-39 bookend may close the whole command list without singling out parental care; both levels remain available.

findings.title: A Measured Force of Speech

findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's transitive rebuke and its commanded noble utterance. The independent triggers are 17:29's full extension of the hand, 17:30's restriction of provision, and 17:35's balance; their contact with the HFT's river and opening-to-flow branches changes simple restraint into an image of force controlled between erosion and nourishment.
findings.reader_payoff: The surrounding measure imagery makes the force of speech perceptible as something that can be released too far or held to a just measure.
findings.containment: Tanharhuma plainly functions as rebuke in the focus; river-cutting and opening-to-flow are remote root branches, and the rain/fertility image is likewise analogical. This is an exploratory material image, never the lexical sense of the verb. The native prohibitions and positive command remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus and later measure cues are supplied, but the flow-to-speech mechanism is a remote, attributed analogy.

findings.title: Lordship as Nurture
findings.claim: Alongside its binding-authority sense, the focus's Rabb title can carry stepwise nurturing: 17:24 invokes the Lord in a prayer for the parents immediately after recalling how they raised the addressee, placing parental care within a sequence where lordship and nurture touch.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is Rabbuka in the focus, for which the supplied branch record includes a nurturing facet. The trigger is the next ayah's renewed address to the Lord and its distinct-root wording for the parents' raising of the addressee; that contact changes a bare authority frame into authority heard alongside sustaining nurture.
findings.reader_payoff: The care command can be perceived within a sequence where divine lordship and remembered parental nurture meet, without making those relations equivalent.
findings.containment: The focus root is ر ب ب while the supplied context root for ربياني is ر ب و. This is a contextual sound-and-meaning contact, not a shared-root or etymological claim, and it does not equate divine lordship with human parenting; the authority reading remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is supplied and accepted, while the context-to-focus nurturing contact is an attributed cross-root inference.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Süreç, gözetilen şeyi eksik durumdan tamamlanmış duruma doğru geliştirir.
branch_activations.carrier: Rabbuka is the focus's divine title, whose supplied branch includes stepwise nurturing and completion.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 17:24 addresses Rabbi in prayer and recalls the parents' rabbayani, their raising of the addressee; the HFT trace locates that form at word 11 with root ر ب و.
branch_activations.activation: The title's nurturing facet meets the distinct-root memory of parental nurture in the immediate sequel.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Lordship can be perceived as sustaining care alongside binding authority.
branch_activations.boundary: The roots remain distinct; no equivalence between divine and human care is asserted.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çocuk yetiştirme, bir mülkü iyileştirme ve yapılan iyiliği tamamlama başlıca uygulamalardır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus carries Rabbuka as the Lord title.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 17:24 explicitly recalls child-rearing and addresses the Lord in prayer.
branch_activations.activation: The child-raising example gives the nurturing branch a concrete contact with the sequel's remembered care.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's Lord title can be heard beside a concrete memory of raising and care.
branch_activations.boundary: This is a contextual resonance, not a claim that Rabbuka means parent.

findings.title: Humility Beyond the Household
findings.claim: The focus's ihsan toward parents becomes one embodied instance of humility: 17:24 lowers the wing toward them, while 17:37 forbids proud walking and recalls the body's inability to pierce the earth or reach the mountains.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's beneficent act toward the parents. The independent triggers are 17:24's lowering posture and 17:37's anti-arrogance command with its physical limits; the contact extends a household gesture into a wider pericope ethic of restraint before the world.
findings.reader_payoff: The lowered posture toward parents can be seen as part of a broader practice of refusing self-exaltation.
findings.containment: 17:37 is general and does not say that its warning is specifically about parents. The link depends on the pericope's bodily contrast between lowering and proud walking; the household reading remains specific.

epistemic.reason: The relevant focus branch and exact native context surfaces are supplied, while the cross-ayah humility relation is an interpretive connection.

branch_activations.activation: The pericope places care for parents beside a later bodily warning against arrogance.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Care toward another becomes a concrete form of non-arrogant conduct.
branch_activations.boundary: This specialization remains one local instance, not the whole meaning of humility.

findings.title: Worship Within Sought Aid
findings.claim: Fātiḥa 1:5 pairs exclusive worship with asking for aid; beside 17:23's coordination of exclusive worship and parental ihsan, that added act lets filial care be heard within the worshiper's dependence on God, without claiming the aid request is specifically for caregiving.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the worship verb under exclusive restriction. The external trigger is 1:5's distinct request for aid, paired with its own worship statement; the repeated worship contact and new aid detail change the reading by adding dependence to the posture in which the care command is received.
findings.reader_payoff: The parental command can be held as responsibility and as a practice carried out from dependence, not self-sufficiency.
findings.containment: The added ayah asks for aid generally and does not name parental care as its object. The native 17:24 prayer and 17:39 worship closure stand independently; this overlay adds one bounded relation without reframing them.

epistemic.reason: Both surfaces and the repeated worship carrier are supplied, but applying the general aid request specifically beside parental care is an inference.

branch_activations.activation: The worship carrier meets an external plea for help, adding dependence to the posture beside the care command.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The care instruction sits beside worship that openly seeks divine assistance.
branch_activations.boundary: The overlay is limited to ayah 1:5 and does not import a whole-surah theme.

friction_notes: The nurture trace at 17:24 word 11 names root ر ب و, matching the supplied context occurrence; its mapped branch root_000537/B005 is registered under ر ب ب. The contextual role is retained as attributed, but this mapping does not independently prove a shared root.

The automatic host basmala and external 1:2-4 repeat lordship, mercy, and evaluation already active in the native pericope; 1:6-7 have no specific focus return. Only 1:5 adds a distinct help-seeking detail, and its relation to parental care remains inferential.
